title: HSL HFP 3-0-0 payload
description: HFP 3-0-0 payload contract. The root validates whether a payload matches one supported event shape without considering MQTT topic context. A field that does not apply in a selected topic context is omitted. Only device-derived values (position, speed, heading, acceleration, odometer, door state, schedule deviation, and battery charge) can be null, and null means only a runtime failure to obtain an applicable value. The topic-aware entry point enforces the context alternatives defined for this version. Schema validation does not establish calendar validity, timestamp arithmetic, complete topic agreement, state transitions, reference-data existence, delivery behavior, or clock synchronization.

schemaVersion.title: Schema version
schemaVersion.description: Exact SchemaVer of this HFP payload contract. This schema accepts only 3-0-0 and rejects other versions, development markers, abbreviations such as "3", and aliases such as "latest". The value identifies the MQTT payload contract, not the MQTT topic version or producer software version.

oper.title: Trip operator
oper.description: Integer identifier of the operator running the trip. This value can differ from the operator in the MQTT topic, which identifies the operator that owns the vehicle. For example, operator Y can run a trip using a vehicle rented from operator X, so the topic identifies X while oper identifies Y. Omit oper when no trip operator applies; it is never null.

veh.title: Vehicle number
veh.description: Vehicle number within the vehicle-owning operator identified by the MQTT topic. The number alone does not provide a globally unique vehicle identity, and the topic's zero-padded spelling does not constrain this numeric payload representation.

tst.title: Event timestamp
tst.description: UTC timestamp recorded at the earliest point in the vehicle software where the data for this MQTT message has been captured. The producer writes exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ and uses NTP leap smearing, so it never emits a leap-second value with second 60. The pattern checks lexical shape only; semantic validation must check the Gregorian date, clock source, and consistency with tsi.

tsi.title: Unix timestamp
tsi.description: Whole seconds since the Unix epoch for the same instant as tst, using the same NTP-smeared UTC clock. The intended relationship equals floor(tst in milliseconds divided by 1000); JSON Schema checks only the integer representation, so semantic validation must check that relationship.

spd.title: Speed
spd.description: Vehicle speed in meters per second. Numeric values must remain nonnegative. Null represents a runtime failure to obtain speed when speed applies; omit the field when it does not apply.

hdg.title: Heading
hdg.description: Vehicle heading in whole degrees clockwise from geographic north, from 0 through 360, or null when unavailable. Whether producers should normalize 360 to 0 remains unresolved.

lat.title: Latitude
lat.description: WGS 84 latitude in degrees, from -90 through 90. Null represents a runtime failure to obtain an applicable coordinate. The final contract has not yet decided whether latitude and longitude must become null together or how null coordinates relate to loc.

long.title: Longitude
long.description: WGS 84 longitude in degrees, from -180 through 180. Null represents a runtime failure to obtain an applicable coordinate. The final contract has not yet decided whether latitude and longitude must become null together or how null coordinates relate to loc.

acc.title: Acceleration
acc.description: Vehicle acceleration in meters per second squared. Negative values represent decreasing speed. Null represents a runtime failure to obtain acceleration when it applies; omit the field when it does not apply. The v3 source signal and sampling interval remain unresolved.

odo.title: Journey odometer
odo.description: Nonnegative meters traveled since the most recent journey or deadrun sign-in, including fractional meters. The counter resets to zero at sign-on and continues through unassigned deadrun and signoff until the next sign-on. VJA captures the post-reset state and requires exactly zero, never null, where an odometer applies. Other applicable events permit null only on a runtime failure. VP retains the counter even for upcoming journeys; modes without an odometer omit it.

drst.title: Aggregate door state
drst.description: Aggregate door state. Value 0 means all monitored doors remain closed; value 1 means at least one monitored door remains open. Null represents a runtime failure or unavailable door-state module and must not receive the meaning of 0. Omit the field when door state does not apply. The exact relationship to door-event trigger timing remains unresolved.

loc.title: Location source
loc.description: Method or source used to determine location: GPS means satellite positioning, DR means dead reckoning, ODO means odometer or route-shape positioning, MAN means manually specified or tracked positioning, and N/A means no location source remains available. The final contract has not yet defined implications between loc, null coordinates, and other unavailable telemetry.

tste.title: Extended event timestamp
tste.description: Draft representation of the same recorded instant as tst, counted in elapsed UTC clock hours from 00:00 UTC on oday and expressed on the same NTP-smeared timescale. For example, oday 2026-09-15 and tst 2026-09-16T01:23:45.678Z produce 2026-09-15T25:23:45.678Z. Hours 24 through 36 make this a custom representation rather than an RFC 3339 date-time. Omit tste when no usable operating-date anchor applies; it appears exactly when oday appears and is never null. Retention, the hour-36 endpoint, and missing, future, or stale operating-date behavior remain unresolved.

desi.title: Line designation
desi.description: Passenger-visible line or route designation, distinct from the internal line descriptor and route identity. Omit desi when there is no passenger-facing assignment, such as contexts where the field is inapplicable; it is never null.

dir.title: Direction
dir.description: HFP trip direction encoded as a string. On normal journeys, value 1 maps to GTFS direction 0 and value 2 maps to GTFS direction 1. Direction 0 is permitted for metro (e.g. deadrun or unassigned context); FIXME: follow up with the data source provider to confirm its exact operational meaning and lifecycle. Omit dir when no direction applies; it is never null.

dl.title: Schedule deviation
dl.description: Difference from the scheduled timetable in whole seconds. Positive values mean ahead of schedule, and negative values mean behind schedule. Null represents a runtime failure to compute an applicable deviation; omit dl when the comparison does not apply, including upcoming VP.

oday.title: Operating date
oday.description: Local operating-day or service-day label in YYYY-MM-DD form. It does not necessarily equal the UTC calendar date of tst because a service day can extend past local midnight. Omit oday when no operating-day assignment applies; it is never null.

jrn.title: Journey number
jrn.description: Internal integer journey number used to identify an assigned service or nonrevenue journey. Omit jrn when the topic context has no journey number; it is never null. Mode-specific availability is documented in the specification.

line.title: Internal line descriptor
line.description: Internal integer line descriptor, distinct from passenger-visible desi. Omit line when the topic context has no line descriptor; it is never null. Mode-specific availability is documented in the specification.

start.title: Scheduled journey start
start.description: Scheduled departure time from the journey's first stop, written as zero-padded local 24-hour HH:mm. This field describes timetable time rather than the event-recording instant and does not use GTFS extended-hour notation. Omit start when no scheduled journey start applies; it is never null.

stop.title: Event-related stop
stop.description: Integer identifier of the stop related to the event, such as the stop from which a DEP occurred, using the same numbering as HFP v2 producers. It does not necessarily equal the MQTT topic's next-stop level. Omit stop when no event-related stop applies; it is never null.

route.title: Route identifier
route.description: String route identity for the assigned route, distinct from passenger-visible desi and internal line. Omit route when no route assignment applies; it is never null. Exact namespace and character constraints remain unresolved.

occu.title: Occupancy level
occu.description: Passenger occupancy level on the HFP v2 scale from 0 through 100. A driver-controlled full-vehicle sign sends 0 while the full-vehicle message is inactive and 100 while the driver has activated it: the vehicle will stop for alighting but will not stop solely to board passengers until the driver removes the message. Producers that measure load might send intermediate percentages. Metro occupancy and load reporting will be handled via passenger counting message channels.

ttarr.title: Scheduled arrival timestamp
ttarr.description: Scheduled arrival time at the event-related stop, written as UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ on the NTP-smeared timescale. It describes timetable time rather than the actual event time. Confirmed retained in HFP v3 for stop and door events and carried by TLR and TLA when the request relates to a stop; omit it when no scheduled arrival applies. Timetable lookups cannot fail, so it is never null.

ttdep.title: Scheduled departure timestamp
ttdep.description: Scheduled departure time at the event-related stop, written as UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ on the NTP-smeared timescale. It describes timetable time rather than actual departure or publication time. Omit it when no scheduled departure applies. Timetable lookups cannot fail, so it is never null. Its TLR and TLA applicability remains unresolved.

dr-type.title: Driver type
dr-type.description: Driver or sign-in type: 0 means maintenance personnel or service technician, 1 means driver, 2 means instructor and remains reserved or reportedly unused, and 3 means no driver signed in. This draft accepts all four values. The events that may use 3 and the sign-out interpretation remain unresolved; the historical v2 sentinel -1 does not validate.

block.title: Block reference
block.description: Integer reference for the selected operating block, as recorded in HFP v2. The field was erroneously listed as blo in earlier draft materials. Omit it when no block assignment applies; it is never null. Namespace and lifecycle remain unresolved.

seq.title: Multi-unit sequence number
seq.description: Sequence number of a constituent unit within a multi-unit vehicle (such as a metro train), starting at 1. Metro messages include this field to identify individual carriages or coupled units. Vehicles without constituent units omit this field; it is never null.

label.title: Vehicle label
label.description: Passenger-visible vehicle label, such as a ferry vessel name. Modes without user-visible vehicle names omit this field; it is never null.

evcp.title: Battery state of charge
evcp.description: Electric-vehicle battery state of charge as a whole percentage: 0 means no charge remaining and 100 means full charge remaining. Omit evcp when battery state does not apply; null is reserved for a runtime failure to read an applicable battery value.

sid.title: Traffic-light junction identifier
sid.description: Technical identifier of the traffic-light junction associated with a priority request. It corresponds to the junction identifier traditionally carried in the MQTT topic. Namespace, range, and TLA payload applicability remain unresolved.

signal-groupid.title: Signal-group identifier
signal-groupid.description: Identifier of a signal group, meaning a group of traffic lights within a junction. Its namespace, scope, sign, range, and uniqueness rules remain unresolved.

tlp-signalgroupnbr.title: Traffic-light signal-group number
tlp-signalgroupnbr.description: Destination or output number within the selected signal group to which the priority request applies. Negative values can occur, so this draft imposes no nonnegative bound.

tlp-requestid.title: Traffic-light priority request identifier
tlp-requestid.description: KAR traffic-light-priority request identifier from 0 through 255. The source wraps to 0 after 255. It correlates a request with an acknowledgment but does not identify messages globally.

tlp-requesttype.title: Traffic-light priority request type
tlp-requesttype.description: Traffic-light-priority request category. NORMAL, DOOR_CLOSE, DOOR_OPEN, and ADVANCE identify the four supported request labels. Their exact trigger and state-machine semantics remain outside this draft pending source-owner clarification.

tlp-prioritylevel.title: Traffic-light priority level
tlp-prioritylevel.description: Requested traffic-light priority: normal requests ordinary priority, high requests elevated priority, and norequest reports that the vehicle suppressed or did not send a request. This draft uses the lowercase v2 spellings and uses this value to select the TLR body branch.

tlp-line-configid.title: Line-level priority configuration identifier
tlp-line-configid.description: Identifier of the line-level configuration used to decide whether to request traffic-light priority. Omit it when no line-level configuration applies; it is never null. Zero sentinels and interaction with the point-level identifier remain unresolved.

tlp-point-configid.title: Point-level priority configuration identifier
tlp-point-configid.description: Identifier of the point-level configuration used to decide whether to request traffic-light priority. Omit it when no point-level configuration applies; it is never null. Zero sentinels and interaction with the line-level identifier remain unresolved.

tlp-frequency.title: Traffic-light priority frequency
tlp-frequency.description: Integer frequency or channel representation used for the traffic-light-priority request. The source material does not yet define its unit, scale, sign, or durable bounds.

tlp-protocol.title: Traffic-light priority protocol
tlp-protocol.description: Protocol used to send the traffic-light-priority request: KAR or KAR-MQTT, following the reviewed HFP v3 workbook labels. The historical v2 label MQTT does not validate in v3; producers must select the label that describes the actual request protocol.

tlp-reason.title: Traffic-light priority suppression reason
tlp-reason.description: Reason that no traffic-light-priority request was sent: GLOBAL means a global rule prevented the request, AHEAD means the vehicle ran ahead of schedule, LINE means a line exception rule applied, and PRIOEXEP means a priority exception rule applied. This draft requires the field only when tlp-prioritylevel equals norequest.

tlp-att-seq.title: Traffic-light priority attempt sequence
tlp-att-seq.description: Sequence number of the traffic-light-priority request attempt. Its initial value, increment rule, reset boundary, wrap behavior, sign, and upper bound remain unresolved.

tlp-decision.title: Traffic-light priority acknowledgment
tlp-decision.description: Acknowledgment for a traffic-light-priority request. ACK means the receiving traffic-light system acknowledged or processed the request message; NAK means it did not acknowledge the request. ACK does not guarantee priority, a green signal, or successful passage.

VP.title: Vehicle position body
VP.description: Vehicle position and status snapshot. The MQTT topic supplies journey type, temporal type, and transport mode, which this aggregate draft does not validate. In mode-specific output, metro vehicles might omit line and jrn and provide seq; ferry vehicles might omit line and jrn and provide label. Publication frequency and telemetry sampling remain operational concerns.

DUE.title: Due body
DUE.description: Event reporting that the vehicle approaches a stop and expects to arrive soon, before entering the stop radius. The distance or time threshold for soon remains unspecified. This draft retains scheduled arrival information from v2 pending a final migration decision.

ARR.title: Stop-radius arrival body
ARR.description: Event reporting that the vehicle enters the stop radius. The radius and boundary-crossing algorithm remain unspecified, and this event does not by itself assert that the vehicle has stopped.

ARS.title: Stop arrival body
ARS.description: Event reporting arrival at a stop after the approach and stop-radius-entry stages. The exact speed, dwell, or position criterion that constitutes arrival remains unresolved.

PDE.title: Ready-to-depart body
PDE.description: Event reporting that the vehicle remains ready to depart from a stop. The precise readiness condition, including any door, timetable, or driver-action requirement, remains unresolved.

DEP.title: Departure body
DEP.description: Event reporting that the vehicle departs from a stop and leaves the stop radius. The radius algorithm and exact relationship to door closure remain unspecified.

PAS.title: Stop-passing body
PAS.description: Event reporting that the vehicle passes a stop without stopping. The detection rule and movement or dwell thresholds remain unspecified.

WAIT.title: Stop-waiting body
WAIT.description: Event reporting that the vehicle waits at a stop. The exact conditions that distinguish WAIT from stop arrival and that start or end the waiting state remain unresolved.

STP.title: Stop-request body
STP.description: Event reporting the first stop-request-button press before a stop. The reset boundary for first, the associated stop, and treatment of repeated presses remain unresolved.

DOR.title: Door-release body
DOR.description: Event reporting door release. The source has not yet established whether release means an enabling command or observed state, which doors it covers, or how it relates to the aggregate drst value.

DOO.title: Doors-opening body
DOO.description: Event reporting that vehicle doors open. DOO remains separate from DOC. The exact aggregate transition, doors covered, trigger timing, and whether drst already equals 1 remain unresolved; the event can occur without an associated stop.

DOC.title: Doors-closing body
DOC.description: Event reporting that vehicle doors close. DOC remains separate from DOO. The exact aggregate transition, doors covered, trigger timing, and whether drst already equals 0 remain unresolved.

TLR.title: Traffic-light priority request body
TLR.description: Event reporting a traffic-light-priority request or reporting that the vehicle suppressed a request. This draft selects request and suppression variants through tlp-prioritylevel. Stop association, configuration identifiers, frequency units, attempt lifecycle, and the final conditional rule remain unresolved.

oneOf.title: Normal-priority request
oneOf.description: Traffic-light-priority request with normal priority. This branch forbids tlp-reason because the vehicle sent a request.

oneOf.title: High-priority request
oneOf.description: Traffic-light-priority request with high priority. This branch forbids tlp-reason because the vehicle sent a request.

oneOf.title: Suppressed priority request
oneOf.description: Report that the vehicle did not send a traffic-light-priority request. This branch requires tlp-reason to explain the suppression. The branch invariant remains subject to source-owner confirmation.

TLA.title: Traffic-light priority acknowledgment body
TLA.description: Response corresponding to a traffic-light-priority request. ACK or NAK describes acknowledgment or processing of the request message and does not guarantee a green signal or successful vehicle passage. Scheduled-departure applicability and topic junction reconciliation remain unresolved.

DA.title: Driver sign-in body
DA.description: Event reporting that a driver signs in to the vehicle. The payload records driver type but no driver identity. Because this event has no operating-date anchor, it omits tste rather than sending null.

DOUT.title: Driver sign-out body
DOUT.description: Event reporting that a driver signs out of the vehicle. Whether dr-type identifies the departing person or the resulting no-driver state remains unresolved. Because this event has no operating-date anchor, it omits tste rather than sending null.

BA.title: Block sign-in body
BA.description: Event reporting that the driver selects or signs in to the operating block that the vehicle will run. Its block property is required and never null because BA records a block assignment. The block namespace remains unresolved.

block.description: The block being assigned by this BA event must be present. Null represents a runtime failure to obtain the assigned block value; omit block only when the event/context does not apply.

BOUT.title: Block sign-out body
BOUT.description: Event reporting that the driver signs out from the selected operating block, historically often at a depot. Its exact relationship to journey or driver sign-out and the value retained in block at the event remain unresolved.

VJA.title: Journey sign-in body
VJA.description: Event reporting that the vehicle signs in to a journey or deadrun assignment. Capture the post-sign-on state: reset the journey odometer before recording this event and emit odo as exactly zero where supported, rather than reading a later live value at publication time.

VJOUT.title: Journey sign-out body
VJOUT.description: Event reporting that the vehicle signs out from a journey assignment, historically after reaching the final stop of a service journey. Final-stop completion and deadrun trigger rules remain unresolved.

EVCHS.title: Charging-start body
EVCHS.description: Event reporting that electric-vehicle charging starts. The physical or software trigger, MQTT context, stop association, driver and block relationship, battery-value availability, and publication behavior remain unresolved.

EVCHE.title: Charging-end body
EVCHE.description: Event reporting that electric-vehicle charging ends. The source has not yet established whether this means unplugging, charger shutdown, reaching a battery target, or another signal; context and publication rules also remain unresolved.

topicAwareMessage.title: Topic-aware HFP v3 validation envelope
topicAwareMessage.description: Validation-only envelope assembled from MQTT topic context and an event body. Exactly one explicit event/journey/temporal/mode profile must match; this wrapper is not sent on the wire.
